newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Up on strong crude, swaps.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Up on strong crude, swaps.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market rose on Tuesday in quiet cargo trading on the back of a strong crude market, traders said.
Firmer prices were also put down to improved bunker demand where supplies are tight. Bunker prices rose by about $2.00 per tonne on Tuesday in fairly active trade.
Unlike in the past, bunker sellers said they were not lowering their offers to entice demand due to the higher replacement costs for their inventories.
Although physical players were sidelined in the absence of incremental spot supplies, the price rise was clearly seen the the swaps market.
August and September swaps were last quoted at $102.50/$103.00 per tonne, from Monday's $101.50/$102.
August traded $103.00 while September traded earlier in the day at $102.25 and $102.50, brokers said.
Traders said also attributed the firmer prices to a reduction regional supplies as well as a cut in exports from the Middle East.
Singapore refiners are processing more lighter crudes or condensates that are rich in light and middle distillate due to the higher prices of those products, they said.

Supplies were also cut in Singapore following the shutdown of Shell Singapore's 11,000 tonne per day (82,000 barrel per day) thermal gas oil complex which produces mainly fuel oil, in addition to gas oil and kerosene.
The unit was shut down on Saturday for a 21-day scheduled maintenance, a company spokeswoman said.
